question: What is the maximum number of ordinary hours an employer may require me to work in a week and in a day?
expected_acts: BASIC CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT ACT 75 OF 1997 (BCEA)
reference_points: BCEA section 9: no more than 45 hours in any week.
No more than nine hours a day if the employee works five days or fewer a week.
No more than eight hours a day if the employee works more than five days a week.

question: How much overtime can my employer make me work, and what is the minimum rate of pay for overtime?
expected_acts: BASIC CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT ACT 75 OF 1997 (BCEA)
expected_facts: except in accordance with an agreement
reference_points: BCEA section 10: overtime only in accordance with an agreement.
Maximum of three hours overtime a day and 10 hours overtime a week.
Overtime must be paid at least one and one-half times the employee's wage.

question: How many days of annual leave is an employee entitled to under the Basic Conditions of Employment Act?
expected_acts: BASIC CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT ACT 75 OF 1997 (BCEA)
reference_points: BCEA section 20: at least 21 consecutive days' annual leave on full remuneration per 12-month leave cycle.
Alternatively, by agreement, one day of annual leave for every 17 days worked or entitled to be paid.

question: How much paid sick leave does an employee get, and over what cycle is it calculated?
expected_acts: BASIC CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT ACT 75 OF 1997 (BCEA)
reference_points: BCEA section 22: the sick leave cycle is 36 months of employment with the same employer.
Paid sick leave equals the number of days the employee would normally work in six weeks.

question: How long is maternity leave in South Africa and when may an employee start it?
expected_acts: BASIC CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT ACT 75 OF 1997 (BCEA)
expected_facts: four weeks before the expected date of birth
reference_points: BCEA section 25: at least four consecutive months' maternity leave.
May start any time from four weeks before the expected date of birth unless otherwise agreed, or on a date a medical practitioner or midwife certifies is necessary.

question: When is a dismissal that is not automatically unfair nevertheless unfair under the Labour Relations Act?
expected_acts: LABOUR RELATIONS ACT 66 OF 1995 (LRA)
reference_points: LRA section 188: a dismissal is unfair if the employer fails to prove a fair reason related to the employee's conduct or capacity, or based on operational requirements.
Or fails to prove that the dismissal was effected in accordance with a fair procedure.

question: What does constructive dismissal mean under the Labour Relations Act?
expected_acts: LABOUR RELATIONS ACT 66 OF 1995 (LRA)
reference_points: LRA section 186(1)(e): an employee terminates employment, with or without notice, because the employer made continued employment intolerable for the employee.

question: What rights does a data subject have under POPIA regarding their personal information?
expected_acts: PROTECTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION ACT 4 OF 2013 (POPIA)
expected_facts: to be notified that personal information
reference_points: POPIA section 5: right to be notified that personal information is being collected.
Right to be notified if personal information has been accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person.
Right to establish whether a responsible party holds their information and to request access.
Right to request correction, destruction or deletion of personal information.

question: If a company's customer database is accessed by an unauthorised person, who must the company notify under POPIA?
expected_acts: PROTECTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION ACT 4 OF 2013 (POPIA)
expected_facts: accessed or acquired by any unauthorised person
reference_points: POPIA section 22: where there are reasonable grounds to believe personal information was accessed or acquired by an unauthorised person, the responsible party must notify the Regulator.
It must also notify the data subject, unless the data subject's identity cannot be established.

question: How long may a business keep records of personal information under POPIA?
expected_acts: PROTECTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION ACT 4 OF 2013 (POPIA)
expected_facts: not be retained any longer than is necessary
reference_points: POPIA section 14: records must not be retained longer than necessary to achieve the purpose for which the information was collected or processed.
Exceptions include retention required or authorised by law, reasonably required for lawful purposes, required by contract, or consented to by the data subject.

question: I signed up for a service after a direct marketing phone call. Can I cancel, and how much time do I have?
expected_acts: CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT 68 OF 2008 (CPA)
reference_points: CPA section 16(3): a consumer may rescind a transaction resulting from direct marketing without reason or penalty.
Notice must be given in writing or another recorded manner within five business days after the transaction was concluded or the goods were delivered.

question: What can I do if goods I bought turn out to be defective a few months after delivery?
expected_acts: CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT 68 OF 2008 (CPA)
reference_points: CPA section 56: within six months after delivery the consumer may return goods that fail section 55 standards, without penalty and at the supplier's risk and expense.
The supplier must, at the consumer's direction, repair or replace the goods or refund the price paid.

question: What standards of conduct must a company director meet when acting in that capacity?
expected_acts: COMPANIES ACT 71 OF 2008
expected_facts: good faith and for a proper purpose
reference_points: Companies Act section 76(3): a director must act in good faith and for a proper purpose.
In the best interests of the company.
With the degree of care, skill and diligence reasonably expected of a person carrying out the same functions, having that director's knowledge, skill and experience.

question: When may a company's board resolve to begin business rescue proceedings?
expected_acts: COMPANIES ACT 71 OF 2008
expected_facts: reasonable prospect of rescuing the company
reference_points: Companies Act section 129(1): the board may resolve to begin business rescue if it has reasonable grounds to believe the company is financially distressed.
And there appears to be a reasonable prospect of rescuing the company.

question: When is a credit agreement considered reckless under the National Credit Act?
expected_acts: NATIONAL CREDIT ACT 34 OF 2005 (NCA)
expected_facts: did not generally understand or appreciate
reference_points: NCA section 80(1): a credit agreement is reckless if the credit provider failed to conduct the assessment required by section 81(2).
Or, having assessed, entered into the agreement despite information indicating the consumer did not understand the risks, costs or obligations, or would become over-indebted.

question: What rights do I have when a government decision adversely affects my rights?
expected_acts: CONSTITUTION OF THE REPUBLIC OF SOUTH AFRICA, 1996
reference_points: Constitution section 33(1): everyone has the right to administrative action that is lawful, reasonable and procedurally fair.
Section 33(2): anyone whose rights have been adversely affected by administrative action has the right to be given written reasons.

question: How do I refer a dispute to the CCMA for conciliation?
expected_acts: Ccma Rules
reference_points: CCMA Rule 11(1): a party refers a dispute for conciliation by delivering a completed LRA Form 7.11 (the referral document).

question: Can an estate agent accept a mandate to sell my house without a disclosure form from me?
expected_acts: PROPERTY PRACTITIONERS ACT 22 OF 2019
reference_points: Property Practitioners Act section 67(1): a property practitioner must not accept a mandate unless the owner or lessor has provided a fully completed and signed mandatory disclosure in the prescribed form.

question: Can my employer treat me unfairly because I am pregnant, and how much maternity leave am I entitled to?
expected_acts: EMPLOYMENT EQUITY ACT 55 OF 1998
BASIC CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT ACT 75 OF 1997 (BCEA)
reference_points: Employment Equity Act section 6(1): no person may unfairly discriminate against an employee on grounds including pregnancy.
BCEA section 25: at least four consecutive months' maternity leave.

question: What rights do workers have to form and join a trade union under the Constitution and the Labour Relations Act?
expected_acts: CONSTITUTION OF THE REPUBLIC OF SOUTH AFRICA, 1996
LABOUR RELATIONS ACT 66 OF 1995 (LRA)
expected_facts: form and join a trade union
participate in forming a trade union
reference_points: Constitution section 23(2): every worker has the right to form and join a trade union, to participate in its activities and programmes, and to strike.
LRA section 4(1): every employee has the right to participate in forming a trade union and to join a trade union, subject to its constitution.

question: What duties does an employer have to keep the workplace safe, and how is workplace harassment defined?
expected_acts: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY ACT 85 OF 1993
CODE OF GOOD PRACTICE ON HARASSMENT
expected_facts: safe and without risk to the health
reference_points: OHSA section 8(1): every employer must provide and maintain, as far as reasonably practicable, a working environment that is safe and without risk to employees' health.
Code of Good Practice on Harassment item 4: harassment is unwanted conduct that impairs dignity and creates a hostile or intimidating work environment.

question: What is the minimum my employer must pay me, and what rate applies when I work overtime?
expected_acts: NATIONAL MINIMUM WAGE ACT 9 OF 2018
BASIC CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT ACT 75 OF 1997 (BCEA)
expected_facts: no less than the national minimum wage
reference_points: National Minimum Wage Act section 4: every worker is entitled to a wage no less than the national minimum wage.
BCEA section 10(3): overtime must be paid at least one and one-half times the employee's wage.
The rand amount of the minimum wage is not in the corpus and must not be presented as grounded.

question: How do the Constitution and POPIA protect my privacy and personal information?
expected_acts: CONSTITUTION OF THE REPUBLIC OF SOUTH AFRICA, 1996
PROTECTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION ACT 4 OF 2013 (POPIA)
expected_facts: integrity and confidentiality of personal information
reference_points: Constitution section 14: everyone has the right to privacy, including not having the privacy of their communications infringed.
POPIA section 19: a responsible party must secure the integrity and confidentiality of personal information through appropriate, reasonable technical and organisational measures.

question: Since the BCEA allows employers to require up to 15 hours of overtime a week, my employer can make me work 15 hours of overtime this week, right?
expected_acts: BASIC CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT ACT 75 OF 1997 (BCEA)
expected_facts: except in accordance with an agreement
reference_points: The premise is false: BCEA section 10(2) limits overtime to 10 hours a week and three hours a day.
Overtime may only be required in accordance with an agreement.

question: POPIA lets companies keep customer personal data forever as long as it is stored securely, correct?
expected_acts: PROTECTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION ACT 4 OF 2013 (POPIA)
expected_facts: not be retained any longer than is necessary
reference_points: The premise is false: POPIA section 14 prohibits retaining records longer than necessary for the purpose of collection, subject to listed exceptions.
Security safeguards (section 19) are a separate obligation and do not permit indefinite retention.
A correct answer explicitly corrects the premise.
